Our story

The Riverside Food Festival started in a small car park behind the old mill, with six tables, two cooks, and a borrowed tent. Nobody expected more than a few neighbours to come by, but by noon the line reached the bridge and the cooks ran out of bread twice. That afternoon, the idea of a yearly festival was born, and the town has kept it going ever since.

Over the years, the festival moved from the car park to the meadow and then to Riverside Park, where it has more room to grow. Today there are more than sixty stalls, run by farmers, bakers, cheese makers, and families who bring recipes from all over the world. Many of them started as visitors, tasted something they loved, and came back the next year with a stall of their own.

We care a lot about where the food comes from. Most of the vegetables are grown within thirty kilometres of the park, the fish comes from the coast, and the bread is baked the same morning in ovens just down the road. We ask every stall to use plates and cups that can be washed or composted, and our volunteers sort the rubbish by hand at the end of the day, so very little ends up in the bin.

Music is a big part of the day. Local bands play on the small stage by the water from the late morning until the evening, and there is a quiet corner under the trees for anyone who needs a break from the noise. Children can join the cooking workshops, plant seeds in the garden tent, and watch the puppet show that has been part of the festival since its second year.

The festival is run by a small team and more than a hundred volunteers, who help with everything from setting up the tents to washing the cups. Without them, none of this would happen, and we are very grateful for every hour they give. If you would like to help next year, our volunteer days start in early spring and we always welcome new faces. A day ticket costs €18 for adults, and children under twelve come in free. The money from tickets pays for the stage, the tents, the cleaning, and a small grant for young cooks who want to start their first stall.

We look forward to seeing you by the river.
